title: Static vacancies as parametrized conformal defects in the critical $J_1$--$J_2$ transverse-field Ising chain
authors: R. L. Silva, R. C. Silva, R. J. C. Lopes, A. R. Pereira
abstract: We revisit the problem of two static nonmagnetic vacancies in the transverse-field Ising chain with first- and second-neighbor couplings $J_1$ and $J_2$, now on the critical line, using density-matrix renormalization-group (DMRG) calculations in open chains of up to $N=300$ sites. In contrast to the gapped regime studied previously, where the vacancy-vacancy interaction decays exponentially, along the entire quantum critical line the interaction becomes algebraic, $|Δ_b(r)|\sim r^{-α}$, with $α$ close to the universal Casimir value of unity and a weak but systematic dependence on the second-neighbor coupling, $α_\infty \simeq 1.070 + 0.091\, J_2/J_1)$ across $J_2/J_1\in[0.1,1.0]$. The transmission ratio of the spin correlator across a vacancy approaches a $J_2$-dependent plateau $T_\infty(J_2)$ that grows from $0.11$ to $0.33$ over the same range, and the Affleck-Ludwig boundary entropy is small and approximately constant, $\log g_\infty \approx -0.073$, well above the Ising fixed-BC value $-\ln\sqrt{2}$ and close to the free-boundary value. The three observables vary smoothly and monotonically with $J_2$, consistent with a one-parameter family of partially transmissive conformal defects controlled by $J_2$. Throughout, the critical line is located using the bulk spin-correlator exponent $η=1/4$, the order-parameter exponent of the Ising universality class, which provides a robust criterion in this open geometry.
summary: This paper uses DMRG simulations on the critical $J_1$-$J_2$ Ising chain to characterize static vacancies as tunable conformal defects. By analyzing the algebraic decay of vacancy interactions, the transmission ratio, and boundary entropy, the authors demonstrate that these three observables vary smoothly with the coupling ratio $J_2/J_1$. This establishes a quantitative link between microscopic parameters and universal defect properties in quantum critical systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how static nonmagnetic vacancies act as parametrized conformal defects within the critical $J_1$-$J_2$ transverse-field Ising chain.
main_result: The vacancy defect forms a continuous, one-parameter family of partially transmissive conformal defects controlled by the ratio $J_2/J_1$, evidenced by the smooth variation of three key observables ($\alpha_\infty$, $T_\infty$, $\log g_\infty$).
method: Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations were performed on open chains, analyzing power-law decay exponents and boundary entropy.
model_or_system: The system is the transverse-field Ising chain with first ($J_1$) and second ($J_2$) neighbor couplings, $H = -\sum_{i} J_1 \sigma^x_i \sigma^x_{i+1} - \sum_{i} J_2 \sigma^x_i \sigma^x_{i+2} - \sum_{i} b \sigma^z_i$, with vacancies acting as defects.
key_observables: Vacancy-vacancy binding energy decay exponent ($\alpha$), spin correlator transmission ratio ($T_\infty$), and Affleck-Ludwig boundary entropy ($\log g_\infty$).
important_parameters: The tuning parameter is the ratio $J_2/J_1$, which controls the defect's properties across the quantum critical line.
main_assumptions: The vacancy is treated as a bulk defect preserving connectivity, and the critical line location is robustly fixed by matching the bulk spin-correlator exponent $\eta=1/4$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the power-law decay of binding energy $|\Delta b(r)| \sim r^{-\alpha}$ (Fig. 2a), plot the dependence of the fitted exponent $\alpha_\infty$ and transmission $T_\infty$ on $J_2/J_1$, and show the extraction method for boundary entropy ($\log g$) (Fig. 6).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model, applies DMRG to calculate three key observables ($\Delta b(r)$, $T(k)$, $\log g$), analyzes how these observables vary with $J_2/J_1$ along the critical line, and concludes that this variation confirms a continuous family of conformal defects.
why_interesting: The work connects concepts from quantum criticality (Ising universality class) to boundary physics via conformal field theory (CFT), providing quantitative evidence for how defect parameters can be continuously tuned by microscopic couplings ($J_2/J_1$).

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The J1–J2 transverse-field Ising chain of Eq. (1) with two static nonmagnetic vacancies a distance r apart. Black spheres are vacant sites; the remaining spins interact via J1 (red) and J2 (green). The J2 bond bridging across each va- cancy (orange) keeps the chain connected and is the channel that gives the defect its J2-dependent transmission.

FIG. 2. (a) The vacancy-vacancy binding energy |∆b(r)| on the critical line, N = 300, for representative J2/J1 values. The behavior is power-law to high precision (linear in log-log over more than a decade in r); 1/r is shown for reference. The fits in the window r ∈[4, 32] all have R2 ≥0.996. (b) The fitted exponent α(N, J2) for the five sizes (colored symbols) and the 1/N-extrapolated α∞(J2) (black stars, error bars from the standard error of the linear extrapolation). The dotted line is the linear fit of Eq. (4); the dashed line marks α = 1.

Figure 2(a) shows |∆b(r)| for N = 300 at five represen- tative values of J2/J1. The data exhibits a clear linear behaviour in log-log over more than a decade in r, demon- strating that the vacancy-vacancy interaction along the critical line is genuinely algebraic, in sharp contrast to the exponential decay found in the gapped regime in Ref. [1]. This is the qualitative change in the vacancy physics in- duced by quantum criticality. A power-law fit in the window r ∈[4, 32] gives, for each (N, J2), an effective exponent α(N, J2) with R2 ranging from 0.996 to 1.000. The values are shown in Fig. 2(b). FIG. 3. (a) Transmission ratio T(k) across a single central vacancy for N = 300 in some representative J2/J1 values. After a short transient at small k, T(k) saturates to a J2-dependent plateau. (b) The 1/N-extrapolated plateau value T∞(J2) (error bars from the extrapolation are smaller than the symbols). The defect is strongly reflective at small J2 (T∞≃0.11) and becomes substantially more transmissive at J2/J1 = 1.0 (T∞≃0.33).

FIG. 5. The Casimir exponent α∞versus the transmission plateau T∞, with point color encoding J2/J1 and error bars showing the α∞extrapolation uncertainty. The two quanti- ties trace a smooth, nearly linear curve, α∞≃0.41 T∞+1.014. Because both are monotonic functions of the single tuning parameter J2, they move together coherently as J2 is varied, with no abrupt features.
